subject.title: Model configuration accepts unvalidated model names, enabling silent misconfiguration

question: Should unknown configured model refs be treated as config validation errors, doctor warnings, or only targeted warnings for retired/suppressed catalog entries?
rationale: The issue is valid, but OpenClaw policy treats config/default changes and fail-closed validation as compatibility-sensitive because strict catalog checks can break custom or future model refs.

options.title: Doctor warning first
options.body: Add advisory doctor/config validate warnings for refs absent from trusted catalogs while keeping runtime forward-compatible behavior.

options.title: Strict config error
options.body: Reject unknown configured refs during config validation and explicitly accept the upgrade risk for custom and future model IDs.

options.title: Suppressed refs only
options.body: Keep the current behavior and only reject model refs that provider manifests explicitly suppress as retired or unsafe.

recommendation.title: Doctor warning first
recommendation.body: Add advisory doctor/config validate warnings for refs absent from trusted catalogs while keeping runtime forward-compatible behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They most recently touched the validation and configured-model-ref collector paths that would host the narrow warning/error decision.
